info.syllabusName: Introduction to International Business_Nhập môn kinh doanh quốc tế
info.timeAllocation: Study hour (150h) = 45h contact hours + 1h final exam + 104h self-study
info.description: Introduction to International Business is designed to equip students with a comprehensive understanding of the fundamental principles and practices of conducting business in a globalized economy. It explores the dynamic interplay of socio-cultural, economic, technological, and political-legal factors that shape the international business environment. Students will gain insights into the strategies and techniques for entering and operating in foreign markets, including trade policies, global supply chains, and cross-border management. A key feature of this course is the integration of artificial intelligence (AI) tools and applications, enabling students to analyze international market trends, optimize decision-making processes, and develop innovative solutions to real-world business challenges. By the end of the course, students will be prepared to navigate the complexities of international business with a forward-thinking, technology-driven approach.
info.studentTasks:
- Attend at least 80% of contact hours in order to be accepted to the final examination

- Actively participate in class activities

- Fulfill tasks given by instructor after class

- Use their own laptop in class only for learning purpose

- Read the textbook in advance

- Access the course website (www.flm.fpt.edu.vn) for up-to-date information and material of the course, for online supports from teachers and other students and for practicing and assessment.

materials.materialDescription: International Business - Competing in the Global Marketplace Global
materials.author: Charles W. L. Hill

clos.loDetails: Recognize the key issues of globalization, and the national differences in political, economic, legal systems and culture
Apply AI to analyze global market trends and consumer sentiment, optimize solutions, and critically address bias, risks, and ethical responsibilities.

Demonstrate understanding about the ethical, corporate social responsibility, and sustainability faced by international business, and explaination how global managers can incorporate such issues into their decision making
Demonstrate understanding about the global trade and investment environment in which international business occurs
Describe characteristics of the foreign exchange market, different theories relating to exchange rate and how to manage foreign exchange risks
Identify the different global strategies and entry modes that firms use to compete in the global marketplace

Explain how firms can perform their key functions including global production, global supply chain management, global marketing, global research and development to compete and succeed in the international business environment
Evaluate external environment of a specific foreign market
Propose the suitable entry mode for a specific company to enter foreign market.
Demonstrate attitude to adapt to differences and complex issues in doing international business
